caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular textile fragment featuring repeating decorative patterns in blue and red on an off-white background. The main composition is divided into square units, each containing stylized motifs of birds, specifically peacocks, perched on tree branches with multiple leaves and flowers. Beneath the peacocks in each square are pairs of smaller birds facing each other. The squares are bordered by floral and foliage patterns, interspersed with circular flower designs in red. The left and lower edges of the textile have multiple bordered bands running vertically and horizontally. These bands contain alternating blue and red geometric and floral motifs, including spirals, leaves, stylized flowers, and small birds within square frames. A fringe of intertwined blue, red, and off-white threads is visible along the left and lower edges. The style is symmetrical, and the arrangement follows a grid-like repetition, primarily using blue and red inks on the textile illustration.
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
